disposition_mapping.rationale: Cutoff enforcement (KB-03) is preserved but re-mechanised: the default all-ready lock is system-executed and logged since it contains no discretionary content, while the not-ready/override decision remains a named, logged human authorisation by the close manager. A resourced manual intake path is added for entities lacking system integration, so the control does not degrade silently for those subledgers.

The council converged strongly (pragmatist, finance_domain, hitl_designer, agentic_architect, accounting_standards, emerging_economy, with maximalist conceding) that mechanical and estimation entries carry different risk profiles and must be distinct named steps, not one step with an internal role split. TS-02 automates template-driven accruals with review-before-post exception handling; TS-03 keeps provisions, NRV write-downs and error corrections human-originated with documented basis (KB-04, KB-05, KB-10), rejecting maximalist's model-originated-estimate proposal in favour of the majority view that automation may only assist, never originate, a judgmental figure.

No KB entry constrains allocation methodology directly, so full automation of the mechanical run is unobjectionable; the one retained human control is sign-off on allocation-base changes, since a basis change is a policy decision, not a calculation, per the shared council view (finance_domain, hitl_designer, agentic_architect, emerging_economy).

Preserves R2R-R-02. The council converged (finance_domain, hitl_designer, agentic_architect, accounting_standards, emerging_economy conceding) that matching and mismatch resolution are a difference in kind, not degree, and must be visible as separate steps so an auditor can distinguish machine-cleared matches from investigated exceptions, strengthening rather than diluting IFRS 10 completeness (KB-14). Unmatched items are force-routed to resolution, never netted away.

Preserves R2R-R-01. Rejects maximalist's proposal to dissolve reconciliation into a merged consolidation/integrity platform: the majority (pragmatist, finance_domain, hitl_designer, agentic_architect, accounting_standards) held that risk-tiering is a single continuum governed by one existing policy, so it remains one step with internal automation for low-risk accounts and full manual certification with evidence for high-risk accounts. Certification must never degrade into a completion-flag rubber-stamp regardless of tier (KB-02).

Consolidation mechanics (FX translation, elimination netting, trial balance compilation) are automated, but against accounting_standards' and the majority's hold, FX translation and exchange differences remain an explicit, separately visible computation rather than reduced to anomaly-only validation (KB-07, KB-08), and methodology/policy drift is flagged distinctly from numeric variance (KB-06). The explicit dependency on TS-06's elimination output is named per finance_domain's and accounting_standards' point.

Preserves R2R-R-07. Every council member treated this as the workflow's core, non-negotiable human judgment checkpoint; only decision-support analytics are added, with no automation of the review, adjustment or sign-off decision. Actor separation from TS-02/TS-03 preparers is preserved structurally, satisfying R2R-R-05.

Preserves R2R-R-06. Mechanical compilation from signed-off results is automated with a tie-out gate blocking distribution on inconsistency; the group reporting accountant's role narrows to commentary and final distribution authority. Ordering is preserved explicitly: reporting compiles only after TS-07 (R2R-R-03) and TS-09 (R2R-R-04) are complete.

steps.description: An orchestration tool monitors the close calendar and subledger (AP, AR, fixed assets, payroll) status feeds continuously. When all subledgers report ready at the scheduled cutoff, the system executes the posting lock automatically as a logged, auditable event and auto-distributes the checklist with owner/deadline tracking — this default path contains no discretionary content and does not require a human click. Where any subledger reports not-ready, or where an entity cannot feed status directly (legacy or spreadsheet-based subsidiaries on a resourced manual/batch intake path), the close manager receives a named exception and holds sole, logged authority to grant a delay or authorise an override past the not-ready condition. The agent may never proceed past a not-ready signal on its own authority.
inputs: Subledger status feeds (automated and manual submission for non-integrated entities)
steps.name: Close orchestration and cutoff control
outputs: Exception/override log with named accountable decisions

steps.description: Recurring accruals and prepayment releases are generated and posted automatically from templates and amortisation schedules within a defined variance tolerance; every posted line carries a traceable link back to its source template/schedule and is reversible via a standard reversing entry, not manual override. Entries deviating from their schedule beyond tolerance are routed to the GL accountant for review before posting, not after. No estimation content is handled by this step.
steps.name: Automated mechanical journal generation
outputs: Mechanical journals posted with template/schedule evidence trail

steps.description: Provisions, bad-debt and expected-credit-loss estimates, inventory NRV write-downs, litigation accruals, reclassifications and error corrections are prepared by a named, accountable GL accountant with a documented basis. Automation may surface trends, prior-period comparisons or candidate model outputs strictly as drafting aids; it may never originate the posted number or substitute for the preparer's judgment. The preparer is a different individual from the Controller performing management review (TS-09), and from anyone who configures automation thresholds elsewhere in the workflow.
steps.name: Estimation and judgment journal preparation
outputs: Estimation-based journals posted with documented basis and named preparer

steps.description: An allocation engine executes shared-service recharges, corporate overhead distribution and intercompany management-fee allocations against the governed allocation model and cost-centre data, auto-posting within a defined tolerance band. Allocation-base changes (new cost centre, revised recharge methodology) are a policy decision and require explicit GL accountant validation and sign-off before use; movements outside tolerance halt the affected line and escalate for review rather than posting an anomalous distribution. A manual validation path is retained for entities supplying lower-quality allocation-driver data.
steps.name: Allocation processing
outputs: Allocation-base changes validated and signed off

steps.description: An automated matching engine reconciles AR/AP mirror accounts, loans and recharges across entities continuously through the period, auto-settling and netting positions that match within tolerance. Every item that does not match is force-routed to intercompany exception resolution (TS-06); no unmatched item is written off, netted or dropped silently. A resourced manual intake path exists for counterparty entities that are not system-integrated, feeding the same evidence store as the automated path.
steps.name: Intercompany matching and settlement
outputs: Intercompany balances matched and settled within tolerance
Unmatched items routed to exception resolution

steps.description: A named intercompany specialist or GL accountant investigates and resolves mismatches requiring inter-entity coordination and judgment, negotiating with counterparty entities as needed, and prepares the elimination entry set for consolidation. Unresolved items are tracked and aged explicitly, never buried in a reconciled-looking status. This step's output is an explicit, named interface feeding directly into consolidation (TS-08), preserving demonstrable elimination completeness under IFRS 10.
steps.name: Intercompany exception resolution and elimination preparation
outputs: Mismatches resolved and aged where outstanding
Elimination entries prepared and signed off

steps.description: Reconciliation matching is automated for low-risk, high-volume accounts against subledger and bank feeds, generating system evidence within tolerance; higher-risk or judgment-dependent accounts retain full manual reconciliation and certification with documented evidence, per the existing risk-rating policy governing frequency and reviewer requirements. The policy-owned risk rating is not alterable by the automation at runtime. Regardless of tier, the certifying reviewer must see aged and unreconciled items with full evidence, not a match-rate completion flag alone — no account is closed by dashboard rubber-stamp. A resourced manual path is retained for entities without automated bank/subledger feeds.
steps.name: GL and balance-sheet reconciliations

steps.description: Trial balance compilation, FX retranslation and elimination netting are executed by a consolidation engine, consuming the elimination-entry set produced in TS-06 as an explicit sequencing dependency. FX translation and exchange differences remain a distinct, separately visible computation at all times, never netted invisibly inside the engine. The financial accountant validates every consolidated balance against entity submissions, investigates deviations beyond a defined threshold, and separately flags any period-on-period methodology or policy-application drift in the consolidation logic itself as a policy question requiring sign-off, not merely a numeric exception. A manual entity-submission intake path is retained for subsidiaries that are not system-native.
steps.name: Trial balance, consolidation and eliminations
outputs: FX translation and exchange differences reported separately

steps.description: The Controller reviews draft consolidated results against expectations and prior period, aided by automated variance and anomaly surfacing that recommends and posts nothing. The Controller investigates anomalies, determines, documents and posts management adjustments, and signs off account-level results. The Controller is structurally distinct from the preparers in TS-02/TS-03 and does not configure the automation thresholds used upstream, preserving independent review.
steps.name: Management review and adjustments

steps.description: Compilation of financial statements, variance schedules and KPI summaries is automated from signed-off consolidated results, with distribution blocked if a tie-out error is detected against the signed-off numbers. The group reporting accountant authors management commentary, including local-context adaptation where relevant, and confirms distribution per the reporting timetable. Compilation and distribution occur only after reconciliation (TS-07) and management review (TS-09) are both complete.
steps.name: Financial reporting package
outputs: Reporting package compiled with tie-out check
